claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch, based on aggregate readiness, staged rollout, rollback capability, monitoring controls, and model-card disclosure, even though the mental health referral routing segment remains below target and exposed.
decision_criteria: Apply the stated policy threshold: exposed material weakness requires either use-case exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance.
Treat rollout percentage, rollback, dashboards, and monitoring as insufficient on their own when the affected segment remains exposed.
Credit admissible support for aggregate readiness and operational controls, but do not let that override the unresolved policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Admissible evidence that the mental health referral routing use case was excluded from the rollout cohort.
A reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record specifically covering the exposed mental health referral routing segment.
The actual model-card language or approval record showing how the unresolved limitation was disclosed and whether certification was conditioned on that disclosure.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance.
The actor summary expressly states the mental health referral routing segment remains exposed and that the admissible record does not show approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, staged rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the missing policy predicate for an exposed weak segment.

Public guidance on monitoring and model cards may support disclosure and ongoing risk management, but it does not substitute for the required exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance in the stated policy.
unsupported_claims: Certification is supportable on a limited basis despite the exposed below-target mental health referral routing segment.
Launch controls and monitoring sufficiently justify certification without evidence that the affected use case was excluded or that reviewed risk acceptance exists.
